_about: Every Policy & Compliance policy, as code: its EARS rule, scope and gate points, with its script beside this file. tools/sync_policies.py compares these with the live pillar and, with --apply, replaces what differs. A new topic's 'projects' seeds its project selection once; after that the selection is managed in the pillar (Dashboard, lws policy projects set).

policies.ears_text: The project's VERSION file shall contain a semantic version in the form <major>.<minor>.<patch>, optionally followed by -dev.<N> or -rc.<N>.
WHEN a commit is made, the commit's VERSION file shall have a higher version precedence than its parent commit's VERSION file.

WHEN a commit is made on a working branch (not master, dev, release/*, hotfix/* or support/*), the commit's VERSION shall be the next patch version of the commit the branch was cut from with the suffix -dev.N, where N is 1 for the branch's first commit and one more than its parent's N for every later commit.

WHEN a commit changes a file under src/ or, in a Unity project, under Assets/, Packages/, ProjectSettings/ or tools/, the commit message shall cite either at least one requirement id in the form REQ-nnnnnnnnn or, if the commit affects no requirement, REQ-NONE (in any letter case); IF a commit message cites REQ-NONE, THEN it shall not cite any requirement id.

WHERE the project is a Unity project, WHEN a commit adds or deletes a file or folder under Assets/, the commit shall add or delete that file's or folder's .meta file with it, and shall not add or delete a .meta file apart from its asset.
WHERE the project's .gitattributes routes files to Git LFS, WHEN a commit adds or changes a file that .gitattributes routes to Git LFS, the commit shall store that file as a Git LFS pointer.

WHEN a commit adds or changes a file, the commit shall not introduce a private key, a provider token or API key in a recognisable format, or an environment file (.env or .env.<name>, other than a template such as .env.example).

IF the newest commit on the integration or production branch is a merge commit, THEN the version control system shall require the first line of that commit to have the form "feat (<issue number or -1>): <title>", "impr (<issue number or -1>): <title>" or "fix (<issue number or -1>): <title>".
WHEN a release or hotfix branch is finished, the system shall merge it back into the integration branch with a non-fast-forward merge.
The system shall propagate a hotfix to the integration branch by merge and shall not propagate a hotfix to the integration branch by cherry-pick.
WHERE another file besides VERSION carries a project's version, the system shall have the VERSION auto-sync pre-commit hook installed and a propagation script registered in version_hooks.

The project shall have the commit-msg git hook that runs its commit-gated policies installed: .githooks/commit-msg shall call `lws policy evaluate --gate-point commit`, and git's core.hooksPath shall point at .githooks.
WHILE the checked-out branch is the production branch, the project's VERSION file shall contain a stable version with no pre-release suffix.
WHEN a production tag is created, the version control system shall create it as an annotated tag named v<major>.<minor>.<patch>.
The system shall ensure that the newest production tag (v<major>.<minor>.<patch>, with no -rc suffix) points at a commit reachable from the production branch.
IF the project's VERSION file carries an -rc.<N> suffix, THEN the checked-out branch shall be a release/* branch.

WHEN a release candidate is cut, the system shall create an annotated tag v<major>.<minor>.<patch>-rc.<N> on the release branch, where N is 1 for the first candidate of a base version and one more than the previous candidate's N after that.
The project's pytest configuration shall register a requirement marker.
WHERE a requirement marker is present in the project's tests, the project shall require that the marker reference an identifier of the form REQ- followed by nine digits.
The project's own Python test suite shall cover at least 90 percent of its statements.
WHERE a project uses issue-driven automation, the project shall contain the .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/claude-task.yml issue form.
The project's git remotes shall use SSH URLs that do not embed credentials.

The project shall carry an AGENTS.md briefing (at the root or as .claude/AGENTS.md) that imports little-workshop's shared briefing section (.claude/little-workshop.md), the generated .claude/rules/claude-instructions.md rule and workshop-lifecycle and policy-preflight skills, and a .claude/settings.json that registers the .claude/hooks/lws_scope_guard.py PreToolUse hook for Bash, the file-edit tools and the little-workshop MCP tools, and shall not carry a CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md or CLAUDE.local.md anywhere.

The project's Claude Code instructions shall load as written: every @path import in an AGENTS.md or a .claude/rules/ file shall resolve to a file inside the project, every rule shall have frontmatter that parses with no field but paths and paths patterns that each match a file in the project, every skill and subagent shall have a description (a subagent also a name), every script a skill names and every hook script .claude/settings.json runs shall exist, no instruction file shall load more than 200 lines, and the instructions a session loads at launch shall total no more than 250 lines.

When a project builds a Python wheel, the wheel's file name shall carry the project's version, in the form <name>-<version>-<tags>.whl, so that the package index can publish it without the version being supplied separately.

The design index blocks and docs/design/README.md shall match what tools/update_design_index.py writes, and Assets/Machination/Schema/machination.schema.json shall match what tools/elm-schema.py writes.
